title.description: Under 60 chars. Imperative action phrase (start with a verb), e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option". Shown as the chip label and the spawned session title.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

cwd.description: Optional. Absolute path to a different project root than the current session's — a path on the host this session runs on. The spawned session gets a fresh worktree under this path. Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

1	"""Estimating the gold grader's error rate with a second independent grader, exactly.
2	
3	The judge-measurement note inverts gold noise at a known flip rate ``eta`` and
4	stops there: ``eta`` must be known.  This module estimates it.  Three raters of
5	a binary truth with symmetric error rates, conditionally independent given the
6	truth -- the gold grader G1 (error ``eta1``), a second grader G2 (``eta2``) and
7	the controller's own answer C (error ``1 - a``) -- have pairwise agreement
8	rates whose polarities ``kappa_ij = 2 A_ij - 1`` factor as
9	``(1 - 2 e_i)(1 - 2 e_j)``, so ``(1 - 2 e_i)^2 = kappa_ij kappa_ik / kappa_jk``.
10	The judge is left out: its errors are correlated with the controller's (that
11	is what ``eps1`` measures), so it is a conditionally independent rater only if
12	A2 already holds.
13	
14	1. Walsh coefficients of the 2^3 label table; the factorization of the pairwise
15	   polarities; exact recovery when the square is a perfect square, an exact
16	   membership test ``eta1 <= eta0`` otherwise, and a 2^-16 bracket by bisection.
17	2. The symmetric model has four parameters on seven degrees of freedom.  The
18	   three polynomial constraints ``M_i kappa_jk = P`` (a rater's marginal bias
19	   times the opposite pair's polarity equals the parity bias), the sign and
20	   range conditions, and tables that violate each.
21	3. A pipeline from a 2^4 record table (controller answer, judge verdict, two
22	   gold labels): ``eta1`` from the three-rater identity, the judge note's
23	   Proposition 2 inverted at that ``eta1``, the judge module's exact tests on
24	   the corrected counts, and the exact propagation of an error in ``eta1``
25	   into ``eps1``.
26	4. The sampling law of ``eta1_hat`` on ``m`` items: the three agreement counts
27	   are a function of a four-category multinomial (two agreements force the
28	   third), so their exact joint law is enumerated in ``C(m+3, 3)`` integer
29	   terms, cross-checked against the ``C(m+7, 7)`` label tables; the exact
30	   probability that the estimator is undefined, the exact moments of the
31	   implied square, brackets on the moments of ``eta1_hat`` itself, the delta
32	   variance as a rational function of the parameters with the (non-diagonal)
33	   covariance of the agreement indicators, a planning size, and an exact
34	   conservative confidence bound from the two graders' disagreement alone.
35	5. The asymmetric (two-class Dawid-Skene) model: a prior and a false-negative
36	   and false-positive rate per rater, seven parameters on seven degrees of
37	   freedom.  The closed-form moment solution in one square root, the label
38	   switching convention, the symmetric model as the special case, the absence
39	   of any equality constraint, and the asymmetric inversion of the judge
40	   note's gold-noise map given the gold grader's two rates.
41	
42	Nothing here calls a model.  Every quantity is a ``fractions.Fraction``; floats
43	are rejected at the boundary.
44	"""
45	
46	from __future__ import annotations
47	
48	from dataclasses import dataclass
49	from fractions import Fraction as Q
50	from itertools import product
51	from math import comb, factorial, gcd, isqrt
52	
53	from spiral_ln.evaluation_feedback_signal import shared_error_bounds
54	from spiral_ln.evaluation_game_feedback import LoopEvent
55	from spiral_ln.evaluation_judge_measurement import (
56	    HALF, JudgeTable, ceiling_p_value, clopper_pearson_contains, expected_table,
57	    fisher_p_value, gold_noise_forward, gold_noise_inverse, independence_p_value,
58	    measurement_ledger, rounded_table, table_estimates,
59	)
60	
61	RATERS = {1: "G1", 2: "G2", 3: "C"}
62	PAIRS = ((1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3))
63	SUBSETS = ((1,), (2,), (3,)) + PAIRS + ((1, 2, 3),)
64	CELLS3 = tuple(product((0, 1), repeat=3))
65	CELLS4 = tuple(product((0, 1), repeat=4))
66	RESOLUTION = Q(1, 2 ** 16)
67	DEGREES_OF_FREEDOM = {"cells": 8, "free_cell_probabilities": 7, "symmetric_parameters": 4,
68	                      "constraints": 3, "asymmetric_dawid_skene_parameters": 7}
69	
70	
71	def _as_q(value, name: str) -> Q:
72	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, Q)):
73	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be an int or Fraction, not {type(value).__name__}")
74	    return Q(value)
75	
76	
77	def _probability(value, name: str) -> Q:
78	    value = _as_q(value, name)
79	    if not 0 <= value <= 1:
80	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must lie in [0, 1]")
81	    return value
82	
83	
84	def _pair(i: int, j: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
85	    return (i, j) if i < j else (j, i)
86	
87	
88	def _others(i: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
89	    return tuple(k for k in (1, 2, 3) if k != i)
90	
91	
92	def _weights(cells, keys, what: str) -> dict:
93	    if not isinstance(cells, dict) or not set(cells) <= set(keys):
94	        raise ValueError(f"cells must map {what} to weights")
95	    table = {}
96	    for key in keys:
97	        value = _as_q(cells.get(key, 0), f"cell {key}")
98	        if value < 0:
99	            raise ValueError("cell weights must be nonnegative")
100	        table[key] = value
101	    if sum(table.values()) <= 0:
102	        raise ValueError("the table needs positive total weight")
103	    return table
104	
105	
106	# --- 1. three raters: the label table and its Walsh coefficients --------------
107	
108	@dataclass(frozen=True)
109	class LabelTable:
110	    """Rational weights on the 2^3 cells ``(x_1, x_2, x_3)`` of three binary
111	    raters' labels: counts or probabilities, nonnegative, positive total.
112	    Rater 1 is the gold grader G1, rater 2 the second grader G2, rater 3 the
113	    controller's answer."""
114	
115	    cells: dict
116	
117	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
118	        object.__setattr__(self, "cells", _weights(self.cells, CELLS3, "(x_1, x_2, x_3) in {0,1}^3"))
119	
120	    @property
121	    def total(self) -> Q:
122	        return sum(self.cells.values(), Q(0))
123	
124	    def probability(self, cell: tuple[int, int, int]) -> Q:
125	        return self.cells[cell] / self.total
126	
127	
128	def walsh_coefficients(table: LabelTable) -> dict[tuple[int, ...], Q]:
129	    """``p_S = sum_x p(x) prod_{i in S} (-1)^{x_i}`` for every nonempty ``S``.
130	    ``p_{i}`` is rater ``i``'s marginal bias ``P[X_i = 0] - P[X_i = 1]``,
131	    ``p_{ij}`` the pair's polarity ``2 A_ij - 1`` and ``p_{123}`` the parity
132	    bias ``P[even parity] - P[odd parity]``."""
133	
134	    out = {}
135	    for subset in SUBSETS:
136	        out[subset] = sum((table.cells[cell] * (-1) ** sum(cell[i - 1] for i in subset)
137	                           for cell in CELLS3), Q(0)) / table.total
138	    return out
139	
140	
141	def agreement_rate(table: LabelTable, i: int, j: int) -> Q:
142	    """``A_ij = P[X_i = X_j]``, directly from the cells."""
143	
144	    if i == j or {i, j} - {1, 2, 3}:
145	        raise ValueError("i and j must be two distinct raters among 1, 2, 3")
146	    return sum((table.cells[cell] for cell in CELLS3 if cell[i - 1] == cell[j - 1]), Q(0)) / table.total
147	
148	
149	def pairwise_kappas(table: LabelTable) -> dict[tuple[int, int], Q]:
150	    """``kappa_ij = 2 A_ij - 1`` for the three pairs."""
151	
152	    return {pair: 2 * agreement_rate(table, *pair) - 1 for pair in PAIRS}
153	
154	
155	def three_rater_model(prior, errors) -> LabelTable:
156	    """Cell probabilities when ``Y ~ Bernoulli(prior)`` and rater ``i`` reports
157	    ``Y`` flipped independently with probability ``errors[i]``.
158	
159	    In Walsh coordinates, with ``tau = 1 - 2 prior`` and ``d_i = 1 - 2 e_i``:
160	    ``p_S = tau^[|S| odd] prod_{i in S} d_i``.  Proof: ``E[(-1)^{X_i} | Y] =
161	    (-1)^Y d_i``, the raters are independent given ``Y``, and ``E[(-1)^{kY}]``
162	    is ``tau`` for odd ``k`` and ``1`` for even ``k``."""
163	
164	    prior = _probability(prior, "prior")
165	    if not isinstance(errors, (tuple, list)) or len(errors) != 3:
166	        raise ValueError("errors must list three rates")
167	    errors = tuple(_probability(e, f"error of rater {i + 1}") for i, e in enumerate(errors))
168	    cells = {}
169	    for cell in CELLS3:
170	        weight = Q(0)
171	        for y in (0, 1):
172	            w = prior if y else 1 - prior
173	            for i in range(3):
174	                w *= (1 - errors[i]) if cell[i] == y else errors[i]
175	            weight += w
176	        cells[cell] = weight
177	    return LabelTable(cells)
178	
179	
180	# --- identification from the pairwise polarities -----------------------------
181	
182	def polarity_squares(kappas: dict[tuple[int, int], Q]) -> dict[int, Q]:
183	    """``(1 - 2 e_i)^2 = kappa_ij kappa_ik / kappa_jk``.
184	
185	    Proof: ``kappa_ij = d_i d_j`` for conditionally independent symmetric
186	    raters, so the ratio is ``d_i d_j d_i d_k / (d_j d_k) = d_i^2``.  A rater
187	    at chance has ``d = 0``, both of its polarities vanish, and the other two
188	    raters are left unidentified (one equation, two unknowns)."""
189	
190	    values = {pair: _as_q(kappas[pair], f"kappa {pair}") for pair in PAIRS}
191	    if any(k == 0 for k in values.values()):
192	        raise ValueError("a rater at chance (kappa = 0) leaves the others unidentified")
193	    return {i: values[_pair(i, j)] * values[_pair(i, k)] / values[_pair(j, k)]
194	            for i in (1, 2, 3) for j, k in (_others(i),)}
195	
196	
197	def exact_square_root(value) -> Q | None:
198	    """The rational square root of ``value`` if it has one, else ``None``.  A
199	    fraction in lowest terms is a rational square iff numerator and
200	    denominator are both perfect squares."""
201	
202	    value = _as_q(value, "value")
203	    if value < 0:
204	        return None
205	    n, d = isqrt(value.numerator), isqrt(value.denominator)
206	    return Q(n, d) if n * n == value.numerator and d * d == value.denominator else None
207	
208	
209	def _square_in_range(square) -> Q:
210	    square = _as_q(square, "square")
211	    if not 0 <= square <= 1:
212	        raise ValueError("no error rate in [0, 1/2] has this squared polarity")
213	    return square
214	
215	
216	def error_rate_from_square(square) -> Q | None:
217	    """``e = (1 - sqrt(square)) / 2`` exactly when the square is a perfect
218	    square (always the case at expected counts with rational rates); ``None``
219	    otherwise.  The sign is fixed by ``e < 1/2``."""
220	
221	    root = exact_square_root(_square_in_range(square))
222	    return None if root is None else (1 - root) / 2
223	
224	
225	def error_rate_at_most(square, bound) -> bool:
226	    """Exact membership ``e <= bound`` for rational ``bound`` without taking the
227	    root: ``e <= bound`` iff ``d >= 1 - 2 bound`` iff (for ``1 - 2 bound > 0``)
228	    ``square >= (1 - 2 bound)^2``; trivially true when ``bound >= 1/2``."""
229	
230	    square, bound = _square_in_range(square), _probability(bound, "bound")
231	    floor = 1 - 2 * bound
232	    return True if floor <= 0 else square >= floor * floor
233	
234	
235	def error_rate_bracket(square, resolution=RESOLUTION) -> dict[str, object]:
236	    """Rational bracket of width at most ``resolution`` around ``e``, by
237	    bisection on the exact membership test; exact when the square is perfect.
238	    The true ``e`` lies in ``(lower, upper]``."""
239	
240	    square, resolution = _square_in_range(square), _as_q(resolution, "resolution")
241	    if resolution <= 0:
242	        raise ValueError("resolution must be positive")
243	    exact = error_rate_from_square(square)
244	    if exact is not None:
245	        return {"lower": exact, "upper": exact, "exact": exact, "width": Q(0), "resolution": resolution}
246	    low, high = Q(0), HALF
247	    while high - low > resolution:
248	        mid = (low + high) / 2
249	        if error_rate_at_most(square, mid):
250	            high = mid
251	        else:
252	            low = mid
253	    return {"lower": low, "upper": high, "exact": None, "width": high - low, "resolution": resolution}
254	
255	
256	def eta_gradient(kappas: dict[tuple[int, int], Q], rater: int = 1) -> dict[str, object] | None:
257	    """Partial derivatives of ``e_i = (1 - sqrt(kappa_ij kappa_ik / kappa_jk)) / 2``:
258	    ``-d_i / (4 kappa_ij)``, ``-d_i / (4 kappa_ik)``, ``+d_i / (4 kappa_jk)``;
259	    exact only when ``d_i`` is rational, else ``None``.  Per agreement rate the
260	    values double, since ``kappa = 2 A - 1``."""
261	
262	    if rater not in (1, 2, 3):
263	        raise ValueError("rater must be 1, 2 or 3")
264	    root = exact_square_root(polarity_squares(kappas)[rater])
265	    if root is None:
266	        return None
267	    j, k = _others(rater)
268	    per_kappa = {_pair(rater, j): -root / (4 * kappas[_pair(rater, j)]),
269	                 _pair(rater, k): -root / (4 * kappas[_pair(rater, k)]),
270	                 _pair(j, k): root / (4 * kappas[_pair(j, k)])}
271	    return {"polarity": root, "per_kappa": per_kappa,
272	            "per_agreement_rate": {pair: 2 * g for pair, g in per_kappa.items()}}

275	# --- 2. the model's testable constraints -------------------------------------
276	
277	def model_constraints(table: LabelTable) -> dict[str, object]:
278	    """Residuals of the three equalities ``M_i kappa_jk - P`` (each is
279	    ``tau d_i d_j d_k - tau d_1 d_2 d_3 = 0`` under the model), the sign
280	    condition (``kappa_ij = d_i d_j`` has zero or two negative pairs, never one
281	    or three), the range conditions (``d_i^2 <= 1`` and ``tau^2 = M_i^2 / d_i^2
282	    <= 1``) and identifiability (every ``kappa > 0`` under ``e_i < 1/2``).
283	
284	    At ``tau = 0`` (balanced prior) every odd coefficient vanishes and the
285	    equalities read ``0 = 0``: they then have no power against dependence."""
286	
287	    coefficients = walsh_coefficients(table)
288	    kappas = {pair: coefficients[pair] for pair in PAIRS}
289	    biases = {i: coefficients[(i,)] for i in (1, 2, 3)}
290	    parity = coefficients[(1, 2, 3)]
291	    residuals = {i: biases[i] * kappas[_others(i)] - parity for i in (1, 2, 3)}
292	    negatives = sum(1 for k in kappas.values() if k < 0)
293	    chance = any(k == 0 for k in kappas.values())
294	    squares = None if chance else polarity_squares(kappas)
295	    squares_ok = None if chance else all(0 <= s <= 1 for s in squares.values())
296	    prior_ok = None if chance else all(biases[i] ** 2 <= squares[i] for i in (1, 2, 3))
297	    equalities = all(r == 0 for r in residuals.values())
298	    signs = negatives in (0, 2)
299	    consistent = equalities and signs and squares_ok is not False and prior_ok is not False
300	    identifiable = negatives == 0 and not chance
301	    return {"kappas": kappas, "biases": biases, "parity": parity, "residuals": residuals,
302	            "equalities_hold": equalities, "negative_kappas": negatives, "signs_consistent": signs,
303	            "chance_rater": chance, "squares": squares, "squares_in_unit_interval": squares_ok,
304	            "prior_in_range": prior_ok, "model_consistent": consistent,
305	            "identifiable": identifiable, "passes": consistent and identifiable,
306	            "vacuous_at_balanced_prior": all(b == 0 for b in biases.values()) and parity == 0}
307	
308	
309	def _rank(rows: list[list[Q]]) -> int:
310	    matrix = [list(row) for row in rows]
311	    rank = 0
312	    for col in range(len(matrix[0]) if matrix else 0):
313	        pivot = next((r for r in range(rank, len(matrix)) if matrix[r][col] != 0), None)
314	        if pivot is None:
315	            continue
316	        matrix[rank], matrix[pivot] = matrix[pivot], matrix[rank]
317	        for r in range(len(matrix)):
318	            if r != rank and matrix[r][col] != 0:
319	                factor = matrix[r][col] / matrix[rank][col]
320	                matrix[r] = [x - factor * y for x, y in zip(matrix[r], matrix[rank])]
321	        rank += 1
322	    return rank
323	
324	
325	def model_jacobian_rank(prior, errors) -> int:
326	    """Rank of the exact Jacobian of ``(tau, d_1, d_2, d_3) -> (p_S)_S`` at the
327	    point: four wherever every ``d_i != 0`` (the three pair rows alone have
328	    determinant ``-2 d_1 d_2 d_3`` on the ``d`` columns), so the model is
329	    four-dimensional inside the seven-dimensional simplex and leaves exactly
330	    three constraints.  With a chance rater the rank drops at a balanced prior
331	    (``tau = 0``) but not at an unbalanced one, where the marginal bias
332	    ``tau d_i`` still moves."""
333	
334	    tau = 1 - 2 * _probability(prior, "prior")
335	    if not isinstance(errors, (tuple, list)) or len(errors) != 3:
336	        raise ValueError("errors must list three rates")
337	    d1, d2, d3 = (1 - 2 * _probability(e, "error") for e in errors)
338	    zero = Q(0)
339	    rows = [[d1, tau, zero, zero], [d2, zero, tau, zero], [d3, zero, zero, tau],
340	            [zero, d2, d1, zero], [zero, d3, zero, d1], [zero, zero, d3, d2],
341	            [d1 * d2 * d3, tau * d2 * d3, tau * d1 * d3, tau * d1 * d2]]
342	    return _rank(rows)
343	
344	
345	def copy_grader_table(prior, eta1, eta2, controller_error, copy_rate) -> LabelTable:
346	    """Labels when G2 copies G1 with probability ``copy_rate`` and otherwise
347	    grades independently at ``eta2``: conditional independence fails.  Closed
348	    form of the residuals: ``r_1 = r_2 = -tau d_C rho 4 eta1 (1 - eta1)``,
349	    ``r_3 = 0``; the failing constraints name the dependent pair."""
350	
351	    prior, rho = _probability(prior, "prior"), _probability(copy_rate, "copy_rate")
352	    eta1, eta2, ec = (_probability(eta1, "eta1"), _probability(eta2, "eta2"),
353	                      _probability(controller_error, "controller_error"))
354	    cells = {}
355	    for cell in CELLS3:
356	        g1, g2, c = cell
357	        weight = Q(0)
358	        for y in (0, 1):
359	            w = prior if y else 1 - prior
360	            w *= (1 - eta1) if g1 == y else eta1
361	            w *= rho * (1 if g2 == g1 else 0) + (1 - rho) * ((1 - eta2) if g2 == y else eta2)
362	            w *= (1 - ec) if c == y else ec
363	            weight += w
364	        cells[cell] = weight
365	    return LabelTable(cells)
366	
367	
368	def copy_grader_residual(prior, eta1, controller_error, copy_rate) -> Q:
369	    """``-tau d_C rho 4 eta1 (1 - eta1)``, the residual of constraints 1 and 2."""
370	
371	    tau = 1 - 2 * _probability(prior, "prior")
372	    d_c = 1 - 2 * _probability(controller_error, "controller_error")
373	    eta1, rho = _probability(eta1, "eta1"), _probability(copy_rate, "copy_rate")
374	    return -tau * d_c * rho * 4 * eta1 * (1 - eta1)

379	@dataclass(frozen=True)
380	class RecordTable:
381	    """Rational weights on the 2^4 cells ``(x_C, v_J, g_1, g_2)``: the
382	    controller's answer, the judge's verdict (``1`` = "correct"), the gold
383	    label and the second grader's label.  Counts on a sealed sample, or
384	    expected counts."""
385	
386	    cells: dict
387	
388	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
389	        object.__setattr__(self, "cells", _weights(self.cells, CELLS4, "(x_C, v_J, g_1, g_2) in {0,1}^4"))
390	
391	    @property
392	    def total(self) -> Q:
393	        return sum(self.cells.values(), Q(0))
394	
395	    def label_table(self) -> LabelTable:
396	        """Marginal over the judge: ``(g_1, g_2, x_C)`` as raters 1, 2, 3."""
397	
398	        cells = {cell: Q(0) for cell in CELLS3}
399	        for (x, _v, g1, g2), weight in self.cells.items():
400	            cells[(g1, g2, x)] += weight
401	        return LabelTable(cells)
402	
403	    def judge_cells(self, gold: int = 1) -> dict[str, Q]:
404	        """The judge note's 2x2 table measured against grader ``gold``:
405	        controller right iff ``x_C`` equals that label, judge right iff its
406	        verdict equals that measured correctness."""
407	
408	        if gold not in (1, 2):
409	            raise ValueError("gold must be 1 or 2")
410	        names = {(1, 1): "right_right", (1, 0): "right_wrong", (0, 1): "wrong_right", (0, 0): "wrong_wrong"}
411	        out = {name: Q(0) for name in names.values()}
412	        for (x, v, g1, g2), weight in self.cells.items():
413	            c = int(x == (g1 if gold == 1 else g2))
414	            out[names[(c, int(v == c))]] += weight
415	        return out

418	def expected_record_table(size: int, prior, accuracy, judge_error, eps1, eta1, eta2,
419	                          copy_rate=Q(0)) -> RecordTable:
420	    """Expected counts for ``size`` items: ``Y ~ Bernoulli(prior)``; the
421	    controller answers ``Y`` with probability ``a``; the judge says "correct"
422	    with probability ``1 - eps0`` on a right answer and ``eps1`` on a wrong
423	    one; G1 flips ``Y`` at ``eta1``; G2 copies G1 with probability
424	    ``copy_rate`` (zero for an independent grader) and otherwise flips at
425	    ``eta2``."""
426	
427	    if type(size) is not int or size < 1:
428	        raise ValueError("size must be a positive integer")
429	    prior, accuracy = _probability(prior, "prior"), _probability(accuracy, "accuracy")
430	    judge_error, eps1 = _probability(judge_error, "judge_error"), _probability(eps1, "eps1")
431	    eta1, eta2, rho = (_probability(eta1, "eta1"), _probability(eta2, "eta2"),
432	                       _probability(copy_rate, "copy_rate"))
433	    low, high = shared_error_bounds(accuracy, judge_error)
434	    if not low <= eps1 <= high:
435	        raise ValueError("eps1 is infeasible for the marginal judge error")
436	    eps0 = (judge_error - (1 - accuracy) * eps1) / accuracy
437	    cells = {}
438	    for cell in CELLS4:
439	        x, v, g1, g2 = cell
440	        weight = Q(0)
441	        for y in (0, 1):
442	            w = prior if y else 1 - prior
443	            right = x == y
444	            w *= accuracy if right else 1 - accuracy
445	            says_correct = (1 - eps0) if right else eps1
446	            w *= says_correct if v == 1 else 1 - says_correct
447	            w *= (1 - eta1) if g1 == y else eta1
448	            w *= rho * (1 if g2 == g1 else 0) + (1 - rho) * ((1 - eta2) if g2 == y else eta2)
449	            weight += w
450	        cells[cell] = size * weight
451	    return RecordTable(cells)

454	def measured_judge_rates(record: RecordTable, gold: int = 1) -> dict[str, object]:
455	    """``a'``, ``eps'``, ``w = W1'/m`` and ``eps1'`` of the table measured
456	    against grader ``gold``, plus the half-up rounded ``JudgeTable`` when the
457	    total is an integer count (``None`` for a probability table)."""
458	
459	    cells = record.judge_cells(gold)
460	    m = record.total
461	    measured_accuracy = (cells["right_right"] + cells["right_wrong"]) / m
462	    measured_error = (cells["right_wrong"] + cells["wrong_wrong"]) / m
463	    wrong_wrong_rate = cells["wrong_wrong"] / m
464	    table, changed = None, None
465	    if m.denominator == 1:
466	        try:
467	            table, changed = rounded_table(cells)
468	        except ValueError:  # every cell rounds to zero: no table to test
469	            pass
470	    return {"cells": cells, "accuracy": measured_accuracy, "judge_error": measured_error,
471	            "wrong_wrong_rate": wrong_wrong_rate,
472	            "eps1": None if measured_accuracy == 1 else wrong_wrong_rate / (1 - measured_accuracy),
473	            "table": table, "rounding_changed_a_cell": changed}
474	
475	
476	def inverted_eps1(measured_accuracy, measured_error, wrong_wrong_rate, eta) -> Q:
477	    """Proposition 2 inverted as one rational function of ``eta``:
478	    ``eps1(eta) = (w (1 - 2 eta) - eta (a' - eps')) / (1 - a' - eta)``.
479	    Proof: substitute ``a - eps = (a' - eps') / (1 - 2 eta)`` and
480	    ``1 - a = (1 - a' - eta) / (1 - 2 eta)`` into the note's
481	    ``eps1 = (eps1' (1 - a') - eta (a - eps)) / (1 - a)`` with
482	    ``eps1' (1 - a') = w``."""
483	
484	    a, e, w = (_probability(measured_accuracy, "measured_accuracy"),
485	               _probability(measured_error, "measured_error"),
486	               _probability(wrong_wrong_rate, "wrong_wrong_rate"))
487	    eta = _probability(eta, "eta")
488	    if not eta < HALF or not 1 - a - eta > 0:
489	        raise ValueError("eta must lie below one half and below 1 - a'")
490	    return (w * (1 - 2 * eta) - eta * (a - e)) / (1 - a - eta)
491	
492	
493	def _sensitivity_numerator(a: Q, e: Q, w: Q) -> Q:
494	    return w * (2 * a - 1) - (a - e) * (1 - a)
495	
496	
497	def eps1_sensitivity(measured_accuracy, measured_error, wrong_wrong_rate, eta) -> Q:
498	    """``d eps1 / d eta = K / (1 - a' - eta)^2`` with the ``eta``-free
499	    ``K = w (2a' - 1) - (a' - eps')(1 - a')``.  Proof: ``eps1 = N / D`` with
500	    ``N = w - eta (2w + a' - eps')`` and ``D = 1 - a' - eta`` both affine, so
501	    ``N' D - N D' = -(2w + a' - eps') D + N = K``."""
502	
503	    a, e, w = (_probability(measured_accuracy, "measured_accuracy"),
504	               _probability(measured_error, "measured_error"),
505	               _probability(wrong_wrong_rate, "wrong_wrong_rate"))
506	    eta = _probability(eta, "eta")
507	    if not eta < HALF or not 1 - a - eta > 0:
508	        raise ValueError("eta must lie below one half and below 1 - a'")
509	    return _sensitivity_numerator(a, e, w) / (1 - a - eta) ** 2
510	
511	
512	def eps1_displacement(measured_accuracy, measured_error, wrong_wrong_rate, eta, delta) -> Q:
513	    """Exact ``eps1(eta + delta) - eps1(eta) = delta K / (D(eta) D(eta + delta))``:
514	    the derivative's denominator with one factor moved to the displaced point."""
515	
516	    a, e, w = (_probability(measured_accuracy, "measured_accuracy"),
517	               _probability(measured_error, "measured_error"),
518	               _probability(wrong_wrong_rate, "wrong_wrong_rate"))
519	    eta, delta = _probability(eta, "eta"), _as_q(delta, "delta")
520	    moved = eta + delta
521	    if not 0 <= moved < HALF or not eta < HALF or not 1 - a - eta > 0 or not 1 - a - moved > 0:
522	        raise ValueError("eta and eta + delta must lie in [0, 1/2) and below 1 - a'")
523	    return delta * _sensitivity_numerator(a, e, w) / ((1 - a - eta) * (1 - a - moved))

538	def calibrate(record: RecordTable, declared_judge_error=None, alpha=Q(1, 20),
539	              resolution=RESOLUTION) -> dict[str, object]:
540	    """The pipeline.  From the 2^4 record: the label table's constraint check;
541	    ``eta1``, ``eta2`` and ``a`` from the three-rater identity (exact or
542	    bracketed); Proposition 2 inverted at ``eta1`` (at both bracket ends when
543	    bracketed -- every inverted rate is monotone in ``eta``, so the ends map
544	    to ends); the corrected expected counts rounded half-up; the judge
545	    module's exact tests on them; the sensitivity of ``eps1`` to ``eta1``.
546	
547	    The tests take the corrected counts as given.  They are an estimate, not a
548	    sample, so the sampling error of ``eta1`` is not in their p-values; the
549	    sensitivity is the first-order account of it."""
550	
551	    alpha = _probability(alpha, "alpha")
552	    declared = None if declared_judge_error is None else _probability(declared_judge_error, "declared_judge_error")
553	    labels = record.label_table()
554	    constraints = model_constraints(labels)
555	    measured = measured_judge_rates(record, 1)
556	    out = {"size": record.total, "constraints": constraints, "identifiable": constraints["identifiable"],
557	           "measured": measured, "declared_judge_error": declared}
558	    if not constraints["identifiable"]:
559	        out.update({"status": "not_identified", "eta1": None, "eta2": None, "accuracy_from_identity": None,
560	                    "inversions": [], "valid": False})
561	        return out
562	    squares = constraints["squares"]
563	    brackets = {i: error_rate_bracket(squares[i], resolution) for i in (1, 2, 3)}
564	    accuracy_identity = {"lower": 1 - brackets[3]["upper"], "upper": 1 - brackets[3]["lower"],
565	                         "exact": None if brackets[3]["exact"] is None else 1 - brackets[3]["exact"]}
566	    eta1 = brackets[1]
567	    points = [eta1["exact"]] if eta1["exact"] is not None else [eta1["lower"], eta1["upper"]]
568	    if record.total.denominator != 1:
569	        raise ValueError("corrected counts need an integer total")
570	    size = int(record.total)
571	    inversions = []
572	    for eta in points:
573	        rates = gold_noise_inverse(measured["accuracy"], measured["judge_error"], measured["eps1"], eta)
574	        closed = inverted_eps1(measured["accuracy"], measured["judge_error"], measured["wrong_wrong_rate"], eta)
575	        if closed != rates["eps1"]:
576	            raise AssertionError("closed-form inversion disagrees with the judge module")
577	        expected = expected_table(size, rates["accuracy"], rates["judge_error"], rates["eps1"])
578	        table, changed = rounded_table(expected)
579	        error = declared if declared is not None else rates["judge_error"]
580	        inversions.append({"eta": eta, "recovered": rates, "corrected_expected": expected,
581	                           "corrected_table": table, "rounding_changed_a_cell": changed,
582	                           "tests": _judge_tests(table, error, alpha, declared is None),
583	                           "sensitivity_d_eps1_d_eta": eps1_sensitivity(
584	                               measured["accuracy"], measured["judge_error"], measured["wrong_wrong_rate"], eta)})
585	    recovered_accuracies = [inv["recovered"]["accuracy"] for inv in inversions]
586	    if accuracy_identity["exact"] is not None:
587	        consistent = all(a == accuracy_identity["exact"] for a in recovered_accuracies)
588	    else:
589	        consistent = (min(recovered_accuracies) <= accuracy_identity["upper"]
590	                      and max(recovered_accuracies) >= accuracy_identity["lower"])
591	    gradient = eta_gradient(constraints["kappas"], 1)
592	    chain = None
593	    if gradient is not None and len(inversions) == 1:
594	        sens = inversions[0]["sensitivity_d_eps1_d_eta"]
595	        chain = {"d_eps1_d_kappa": {pair: sens * g for pair, g in gradient["per_kappa"].items()},
596	                 "d_eps1_d_agreement": {pair: sens * g for pair, g in gradient["per_agreement_rate"].items()}}
597	    out.update({"status": "exact" if len(points) == 1 else "bracketed",
598	                "squares": squares, "eta1": eta1, "eta2": brackets[2],
599	                "accuracy_from_identity": accuracy_identity, "accuracy_consistent": consistent,
600	                "inversions": inversions, "eta_gradient": gradient, "chain_sensitivity": chain,
601	                "valid": constraints["passes"]})
602	    return out

613	
614	PATTERNS = ("all", (1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3))
615	ROOT_BITS = 16

617	
618	def _three(values, name: str) -> tuple[Q, Q, Q]:
619	    if not isinstance(values, (tuple, list)) or len(values) != 3:
620	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must list three rates")
621	    return tuple(_probability(v, f"{name}[{i}]") for i, v in enumerate(values))
622	
623	
624	def _size(value) -> int:
625	    if type(value) is not int or value < 1:
626	        raise ValueError("size must be a positive integer")
627	    return value
628	
629	
630	def _rate_pair(value, name: str) -> tuple[Q, Q]:
631	    """A rater's ``(false_negative, false_positive)`` pair of probabilities."""
632	
633	    if not isinstance(value, (tuple, list)) or len(value) != 2:
634	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a pair (false_negative, false_positive)")
635	    return _probability(value[0], f"{name} false_negative"), _probability(value[1], f"{name} false_positive")

637	
638	def root_bracket(value, bits: int = ROOT_BITS) -> dict[str, object]:
639	    """``sqrt(value)`` exactly when rational, else the bracket
640	    ``[r / 2^bits, (r + 1) / 2^bits)`` with ``r = isqrt(floor(value 4^bits))``:
641	    an exact integer statement, since ``floor(sqrt(floor(x))) = floor(sqrt(x))``
642	    for ``x >= 0``.  Agrees with the bisection bracket of ``error_rate_bracket``."""
643	
644	    value = _as_q(value, "value")
645	    if value < 0 or type(bits) is not int or bits < 1:
646	        raise ValueError("value must be nonnegative and bits a positive integer")
647	    exact = exact_square_root(value)
648	    if exact is not None:
649	        return {"lower": exact, "upper": exact, "exact": exact, "width": Q(0)}
650	    r = isqrt((value.numerator << (2 * bits)) // value.denominator)
651	    return {"lower": Q(r, 1 << bits), "upper": Q(r + 1, 1 << bits), "exact": None, "width": Q(1, 1 << bits)}
652	
653	
654	def agreement_patterns(table: LabelTable) -> dict[object, Q]:
655	    """Per item the agreement indicators ``(I_12, I_13, I_23)`` take one of
656	    four values, ``(1,1,1)`` (``"all"``), ``(1,0,0)``, ``(0,1,0)``, ``(0,0,1)``:
657	    two agreements force the third.  ``q_all = p(000) + p(111) = (1 + kappa_12
658	    + kappa_13 + kappa_23) / 4`` and ``q_ij = A_ij - q_all`` depend on the table
659	    only through the kappas, so under the model the law of any function of the
660	    agreement counts is free of the prior."""
661	
662	    q = {name: Q(0) for name in PATTERNS}
663	    for cell in CELLS3:
664	        a, b, c = cell
665	        key = "all" if a == b == c else (1, 2) if a == b else (1, 3) if a == c else (2, 3)
666	        q[key] += table.probability(cell)
667	    return q
668	
669	
670	def agreement_covariance(table: LabelTable) -> dict[tuple, Q]:
671	    """Per-item covariance of ``(I_12, I_13, I_23)``: ``Var I_ij = (1 -
672	    kappa_ij^2) / 4`` and ``Cov(I_ij, I_ik) = q_all - A_ij A_ik = (kappa_jk -
673	    kappa_ij kappa_ik) / 4`` for any distribution; the sample agreement rates
674	    on ``m`` items have covariance ``Sigma / m``.  Not diagonal."""
675	
676	    kappas = pairwise_kappas(table)
677	    q_all = agreement_patterns(table)["all"]
678	    return {(p, r): (1 - kappas[p] ** 2) / 4 if p == r else q_all - (1 + kappas[p]) * (1 + kappas[r]) / 4
679	            for p in PAIRS for r in PAIRS}
680	
681	
682	def agreement_covariance_model(errors) -> dict[tuple, Q]:
683	    """The same matrix under the model: ``Cov(I_ij, I_ik) = d_j d_k (1 - d_i^2) / 4``
684	    (``kappa_jk - kappa_ij kappa_ik = d_j d_k - d_i^2 d_j d_k``) and
685	    ``Var I_ij = (1 - d_i^2 d_j^2) / 4``."""
686	
687	    d = {i + 1: 1 - 2 * e for i, e in enumerate(_three(errors, "errors"))}
688	    out = {}
689	    for p in PAIRS:
690	        for r in PAIRS:
691	            if p == r:
692	                out[(p, r)] = (1 - (d[p[0]] * d[p[1]]) ** 2) / 4
693	            else:
694	                (i,) = set(p) & set(r)
695	                j, k = _others(i)
696	                out[(p, r)] = d[j] * d[k] * (1 - d[i] ** 2) / 4
697	    return out
698	
699	
700	def delta_variance(errors) -> dict[str, object]:
701	    """Asymptotic ``m Var(eta1_hat) -> V = g^T Sigma g`` with the gradient per
702	    agreement rate ``g = (-1/(2 d_2), -1/(2 d_3), d_1/(2 d_2 d_3))`` (twice the
703	    per-kappa gradient of ``eta_gradient``) and ``Sigma`` the model covariance:
704	
705	    ``V = (d_1^2 + d_2^2 + d_3^2 - 2 d_1^2 d_2^2 - 2 d_1^2 d_3^2 + 2 d_2^2 d_3^2
706	    - d_1^2 d_2^2 d_3^2) / (16 d_2^2 d_3^2)``.
707	
708	    The square ``S = (1 - 2 eta_1)^2 = kappa_12 kappa_13 / kappa_23`` has
709	    gradient ``-4 d_1 g``, so ``m Var(S_hat) -> 16 d_1^2 V``.  Every rater
710	    must be better than chance: at ``d_1 = 0`` the root is not differentiable
711	    and the estimator is undefined with probability bounded away from zero."""
712	
713	    errors = _three(errors, "errors")
714	    d1, d2, d3 = (1 - 2 * e for e in errors)
715	    if not (d1 > 0 and d2 > 0 and d3 > 0):
716	        raise ValueError("the delta method needs every error rate below one half")
717	    gradient = {(1, 2): -1 / (2 * d2), (1, 3): -1 / (2 * d3), (2, 3): d1 / (2 * d2 * d3)}
718	    sigma = agreement_covariance_model(errors)
719	    quadratic = sum((gradient[p] * sigma[(p, r)] * gradient[r] for p in PAIRS for r in PAIRS), Q(0))
720	    numerator = (d1 ** 2 + d2 ** 2 + d3 ** 2 - 2 * d1 ** 2 * d2 ** 2 - 2 * d1 ** 2 * d3 ** 2
721	                 + 2 * d2 ** 2 * d3 ** 2 - d1 ** 2 * d2 ** 2 * d3 ** 2)
722	    closed = numerator / (16 * d2 ** 2 * d3 ** 2)
723	    if closed != quadratic:
724	        raise AssertionError("closed form of the delta variance disagrees with g^T Sigma g")
725	    return {"eta": closed, "square": 16 * d1 ** 2 * closed, "gradient_per_agreement_rate": gradient,
726	            "covariance": sigma, "numerator": numerator, "root_of_eta_variance": exact_square_root(closed)}
727	
728	
729	def delta_variance_from_table(table: LabelTable, rater: int = 1) -> Q | None:
730	    """``g^T Sigma g`` from a table alone, ``g`` from ``eta_gradient`` (exact
731	    only when the square is perfect) and ``Sigma`` from ``agreement_covariance``."""
732	
733	    gradient = eta_gradient(pairwise_kappas(table), rater)
734	    if gradient is None:
735	        return None
736	    g, sigma = gradient["per_agreement_rate"], agreement_covariance(table)
737	    return sum((g[p] * sigma[(p, r)] * g[r] for p in PAIRS for r in PAIRS), Q(0))

740	def planning_size(errors, target_se) -> int:
741	    """Smallest ``m`` with delta standard error ``sqrt(V / m) < target``:
742	    ``floor(V / target^2) + 1``."""
743	
744	    target = _as_q(target_se, "target_se")
745	    if target <= 0:
746	        raise ValueError("target_se must be positive")
747	    v = delta_variance(errors)["eta"]
748	    return int(v / target ** 2) + 1

751	def _pattern_integers(errors) -> tuple[dict, int]:
752	    q = agreement_patterns(three_rater_model(HALF, _three(errors, "errors")))
753	    den = 1
754	    for v in q.values():
755	        den = den * v.denominator // gcd(den, v.denominator)
756	    return {k: int(v * den) for k, v in q.items()}, den

759	def _law_summary(m: int, eta1: Q, tolerance: Q, bits: int, total: int, w: dict, acc_num: dict,
760	                 acc_num2: dict, acc_root: int, square_distribution: dict | None) -> dict[str, object]:
761	    w_def = w["exact"] + w["bracketed"]
762	    out = {"size": m, "eta1": eta1, "tolerance": tolerance,
763	           "p_undefined_sign": Q(w["sign"], total), "p_undefined_range": Q(w["range"], total),
764	           "p_undefined": Q(w["sign"] + w["range"], total), "p_exact": Q(w["exact"], total),
765	           "p_bracketed": Q(w["bracketed"], total), "p_defined": Q(w_def, total),
766	           "p_within_tolerance": Q(w["within"], total),
767	           "p_within_tolerance_given_defined": None if w_def == 0 else Q(w["within"], w_def)}
768	    if w_def == 0:
769	        out.update({"square_mean": None, "square_variance": None})
770	        return out
771	    es = sum((Q(v, m * d) for d, v in acc_num.items()), Q(0)) / w_def
772	    es2 = sum((Q(v, (m * d) ** 2) for d, v in acc_num2.items()), Q(0)) / w_def
773	    root_lo, root_hi = Q(acc_root, w_def << bits), Q(acc_root + w_def, w_def << bits)
774	    out.update({"square_mean": es, "square_variance": es2 - es * es, "scaled_square_variance": m * (es2 - es * es),
775	                "root_mean_bracket": (root_lo, root_hi),
776	                "eta_mean_bracket": ((1 - root_hi) / 2, (1 - root_lo) / 2),
777	                "eta_variance_bracket": ((es - root_hi ** 2) / 4, (es - root_lo ** 2) / 4),
778	                "scaled_eta_variance_bracket": (m * (es - root_hi ** 2) / 4, m * (es - root_lo ** 2) / 4),
779	                "moments_are": "conditional on the estimator being defined",
780	                "square_distribution": square_distribution})
781	    return out

784	def _tolerance_bounds(eta1: Q, tolerance: Q) -> tuple[Q, Q]:
785	    """``|eta_hat - eta1| <= tol`` iff ``lo <= S_hat <= hi`` with ``lo = max(0,
786	    1 - 2(eta1 + tol))^2`` and ``hi = min(1, 1 - 2(eta1 - tol))^2``."""
787	
788	    low_root, high_root = max(Q(0), 1 - 2 * (eta1 + tolerance)), min(Q(1), 1 - 2 * (eta1 - tolerance))
789	    return low_root ** 2, high_root ** 2
790	
791	
792	def sampling_law(size, errors, tolerance=Q(1, 50), bits: int = ROOT_BITS) -> dict[str, object]:
793	    """Exact law of ``eta1_hat`` on ``m`` items, free of the prior, by
794	    enumerating the ``C(m+3, 3)`` compositions of the four-category multinomial
795	    of agreement patterns (integer weights over a common denominator ``D^m``).
796	
797	    Outcome classes: some ``kappa_hat <= 0`` (sign; undefined), all positive
798	    but ``S_hat > 1`` (range; undefined), ``S_hat`` a perfect square (exact
799	    ``eta1_hat``) and otherwise (bracketed).  Moments of ``S_hat`` and of
800	    ``eta1_hat`` are conditional on the defined event; those of ``eta1_hat``
801	    are brackets, from ``root_bracket`` at ``2^-bits`` per outcome.  Also the
802	    exact probability that the estimator is defined and within ``tolerance``
803	    of ``eta1``."""
804	
805	    m, errors, tolerance = _size(size), _three(errors, "errors"), _probability(tolerance, "tolerance")
806	    n, den = _pattern_integers(errors)
807	    n0, n12, n13, n23 = n["all"], n[(1, 2)], n[(1, 3)], n[(2, 3)]
808	    pw = {name: [1] * (m + 1) for name in ("0", "12", "13", "23")}
809	    for name, base in (("0", n0), ("12", n12), ("13", n13), ("23", n23)):
810	        for k in range(1, m + 1):
811	            pw[name][k] = pw[name][k - 1] * base
812	    fact = [factorial(k) for k in range(m + 1)]
813	    choose = [[comb(r, j) for j in range(r + 1)] for r in range(m + 1)]
814	    lo_sq, hi_sq = _tolerance_bounds(errors[0], tolerance)
815	    lo_n, lo_d, hi_n, hi_d = lo_sq.numerator, lo_sq.denominator, hi_sq.numerator, hi_sq.denominator
816	    shift = 2 * bits
817	    w = {"sign": 0, "range": 0, "exact": 0, "bracketed": 0, "within": 0}
818	    acc_num, acc_num2, acc_root, total = {}, {}, 0, 0
819	    for k23 in range(m + 1):
820	        for k0 in range(m - k23 + 1):
821	            rest = m - k23 - k0
822	            d = 2 * (k0 + k23) - m
823	            dd = m * d
824	            outer = fact[m] // (fact[k23] * fact[k0] * fact[rest]) * pw["23"][k23] * pw["0"][k0]
825	            row, p12, p13 = choose[rest], pw["12"], pw["13"]
826	            s_num = s_num2 = 0
827	            for k12 in range(rest + 1):
828	                weight = outer * row[k12] * p12[k12] * p13[rest - k12]
829	                total += weight
830	                a, b = 2 * (k0 + k12) - m, 2 * (k0 + rest - k12) - m
831	                if a <= 0 or b <= 0 or d <= 0:
832	                    w["sign"] += weight
833	                    continue
834	                num = a * b
835	                if num > dd:
836	                    w["range"] += weight
837	                    continue
838	                s_num += weight * num
839	                s_num2 += weight * num * num
840	                g = gcd(num, dd)
841	                nn, dn = num // g, dd // g
842	                rn, rd = isqrt(nn), isqrt(dn)
843	                w["exact" if rn * rn == nn and rd * rd == dn else "bracketed"] += weight

272	def _count_moments(m, errors):
273	    """Exact first and second moments of the agreement counts by listing every
274	    assignment of ``m`` items to the eight cells (``8^m`` sequences)."""
275	
276	    table = three_rater_model(Q(1, 3), errors)
277	    first = {pair: Q(0) for pair in PAIRS}
278	    second = {(p, r): Q(0) for p in PAIRS for r in PAIRS}
279	    for items in product(CELLS3, repeat=m):
280	        weight = Q(1)
281	        for cell in items:
282	            weight *= table.probability(cell)
283	        counts = {pair: sum(1 for cell in items if cell[pair[0] - 1] == cell[pair[1] - 1]) for pair in PAIRS}
284	        for p in PAIRS:
285	            first[p] += weight * counts[p]
286	            for r in PAIRS:
287	                second[(p, r)] += weight * counts[p] * counts[r]
288	    return {(p, r): second[(p, r)] - first[p] * first[r] for p in PAIRS for r in PAIRS}

394	def _enumerate_ds(prior, fn, fp):
395	    cells = {cell: Q(0) for cell in CELLS3}
396	    for y, x1, x2, x3 in product((0, 1), repeat=4):
397	        w = prior if y else 1 - prior
398	        for x, a, b in zip((x1, x2, x3), fn, fp):
399	            hit = (1 - a) if y else b
400	            w *= hit if x == 1 else 1 - hit
401	        cells[(x1, x2, x3)] += w
402	    return cells

405	def _enumerate_record_asymmetric(prior, controller, judge_error, eps1, gold, second):
406	    acc = {1: 1 - controller[0], 0: 1 - controller[1]}
407	    accuracy = prior * acc[1] + (1 - prior) * acc[0]
408	    eps0 = (judge_error - (1 - accuracy) * eps1) / accuracy
409	    cells = {}
410	    for y, x, v, g1, g2 in product((0, 1), repeat=5):
411	        w = prior if y else 1 - prior
412	        right = x == y
413	        w *= acc[y] if right else 1 - acc[y]
414	        says = (1 - eps0) if right else eps1
415	        w *= says if v else 1 - says
416	        for g, (a, b) in ((g1, gold), (g2, second)):
417	            hit = (1 - a) if y else b
418	            w *= hit if g == 1 else 1 - hit
419	        cells[(x, v, g1, g2)] = cells.get((x, v, g1, g2), Q(0)) + w
420	    return cells

918	def _binomial_upper_tail(trials: int, p: Q, k: int) -> Q:
919	    """``P(Bin(n, p) >= k)`` by integer accumulation over the common
920	    denominator ``b^n`` (``p = a/b``, ``c = b - a``): the terms ``t_j = C(n, j)
921	    a^j c^(n-j)`` satisfy ``t_{j+1} = t_j (n - j) a / ((j + 1) c)`` exactly, so
922	    one small multiplication and one exact small division per term.  Equals
923	    the judge module's tail."""
924	
925	    a, b = p.numerator, p.denominator
926	    c = b - a
927	    if k <= 0:
928	        return Q(1)
929	    if k > trials or a == 0:
930	        return Q(0)
931	    if c == 0:
932	        return Q(1)
933	    term = comb(trials, k) * a ** k * c ** (trials - k)
934	    acc = term
935	    for j in range(k, trials):
936	        term = term * (trials - j) * a // ((j + 1) * c)
937	        acc += term
938	    return Q(acc, b ** trials)

947	    ``d_2 <= 1``: ``eta_1 <= 1 - A_L``, likewise ``eta_2 <= 1 - A_L``.  It bounds
948	    each grader's error by the pair's disagreement; it gives no lower bound,

994	    """Cell probabilities when ``Y ~ Bernoulli(prior)`` and rater ``i`` reports
995	    ``X_i = 0`` with probability ``alpha_i`` when ``Y = 1`` and ``X_i = 1``

1004	def dawid_skene_moments(table: LabelTable) -> dict[str, object]:
1005	    """``p_i = P[X_i = 1]``, the pair covariances ``c_ij = p_ij - p_i p_j`` and
1006	    the third central moment ``k_3 = E prod (X_i - p_i) = p_123 - sum_i p_i
1007	    p_jk + 2 p_1 p_2 p_3``.  Under the model, with ``u = pi (1 - pi)`` and
1008	    ``delta_i = 1 - alpha_i - beta_i``: ``c_ij = u delta_i delta_j`` (rank one)
1009	    and ``k_3 = u (1 - 2 pi) delta_1 delta_2 delta_3``, so the radicand
1010	    ``k_3^2 + 4 c_12 c_13 c_23 = (u delta_1 delta_2 delta_3)^2``."""
1011	
1012	    p = {i: sum((table.probability(c) for c in CELLS3 if c[i - 1] == 1), Q(0)) for i in (1, 2, 3)}
1013	    pp = {pair: sum((table.probability(c) for c in CELLS3 if c[pair[0] - 1] == 1 and c[pair[1] - 1] == 1), Q(0))
1014	          for pair in PAIRS}
1015	    p123 = table.probability((1, 1, 1))
1016	    cov = {pair: pp[pair] - p[pair[0]] * p[pair[1]] for pair in PAIRS}
1017	    third = p123 - sum(p[i] * pp[_others(i)] for i in (1, 2, 3)) + 2 * p[1] * p[2] * p[3]
1018	    radicand = third ** 2 + 4 * cov[(1, 2)] * cov[(1, 3)] * cov[(2, 3)]
1019	    return {"marginals": p, "pair_moments": pp, "triple_moment": p123, "covariances": cov,
1020	            "third_cumulant": third, "radicand": radicand}

1023	def _ds_parameters(moments: dict, root: Q, sigma: int) -> dict[str, object]:
1024	    """Under ``delta_1 > 0`` with ``sigma = sign(c_23)``: ``pi = (R - sigma k_3)
1025	    / (2R)``, ``delta_1 = R / |c_23|``, ``delta_2 = sigma R / c_13``, ``delta_3 =
1026	    sigma R / c_12``, ``1 - alpha_i = p_i + (1 - pi) delta_i``, ``beta_i = p_i
1027	    - pi delta_i``.  Proof: ``R = u |delta_1 delta_2 delta_3|`` and ``k_3 / c_23
1028	    = (1 - 2 pi) delta_1``, so ``1 - alpha_1 - p_1`` and ``beta_1 - p_1`` are the
1029	    roots ``(1 - pi) delta_1`` and ``-pi delta_1`` of ``z^2 - (k_3 / c_23) z -
1030	    c_12 c_13 / c_23``; every parameter but ``pi`` is affine in ``R`` and ``pi``
1031	    is monotone in it."""
1032	
1033	    p, cov, third = moments["marginals"], moments["covariances"], moments["third_cumulant"]
1034	    prior = (root - sigma * third) / (2 * root)
1035	    delta = {1: root / abs(cov[(2, 3)]), 2: sigma * root / cov[(1, 3)], 3: sigma * root / cov[(1, 2)]}

1037	    beta = {i: p[i] - prior * delta[i] for i in (1, 2, 3)}
1038	    return {"prior": prior, "false_negatives": {i: 1 - sens[i] for i in (1, 2, 3)}, "false_positives": beta,
1039	            "deltas": delta}

1223	    e_b = sum(weight[y] * (1 - 2 * flip[y]) * (1 - acc[y]) for y in (0, 1))

1225	    g_b = sum(weight[y] * (1 - acc[y]) * (1 - flip[y]) for y in (0, 1))
1226	    determinant = e_a * g_b + e_b * g_a
1227	    if determinant == 0:
1228	        raise ValueError("the inversion is singular (a degenerate controller or a gold grader at chance)")
1229	    eps1 = (e_a * (w - g_a) + g_a * (e_m - f_bar)) / determinant
1230	    eps0 = (g_b * (e_m - f_bar) - e_b * (w - g_a)) / determinant
1231	    accuracy = prior * acc[1] + (1 - prior) * acc[0]
1232	    predicted = sum(weight[y] * (acc[y] * (1 - flip[y]) + (1 - acc[y]) * flip[y]) for y in (0, 1))
1233	    return {"accuracy": accuracy, "eps0": eps0, "eps1": eps1,
1234	            "judge_error": accuracy * eps0 + (1 - accuracy) * eps1,
1235	            "determinant": determinant, "measured_accuracy_consistent": predicted == a_m}

1238	def calibrate_asymmetric(record: RecordTable, declared_judge_error=None, alpha=Q(1, 20),
1239	                         convention: str = "all_informative", bits: int = ROOT_BITS) -> dict[str, object]:
1240	    """The pipeline under the asymmetric model: Dawid-Skene fit of the label
1241	    table, the asymmetric inversion at the fitted rates, corrected counts and
1242	    the judge module's tests.  When the fit is bracketed the inversion is
1243	    evaluated at both ends of the root's bracket; those are the ends of the
1244	    ``eps1`` bracket only if the inversion is monotone in the root, which is
1245	    not checked here."""
1246	
1247	    alpha = _probability(alpha, "alpha")
1248	    declared = None if declared_judge_error is None else _probability(declared_judge_error, "declared_judge_error")
1249	    if record.total.denominator != 1:
1250	        raise ValueError("corrected counts need an integer total")
1251	    size = int(record.total)
1252	    fit = dawid_skene_three_raters(record.label_table(), convention, bits)
1253	    measured = measured_judge_rates(record, 1)
1254	    out = {"size": record.total, "fit": fit, "measured": measured, "declared_judge_error": declared,
1255	           "symmetric_constraints": model_constraints(record.label_table())}
1256	    if fit["status"] not in ("exact", "bracketed") or not fit["in_range"]:
1257	        out.update({"status": "out_of_range" if fit["status"] in ("exact", "bracketed") else fit["status"],
1258	                    "inversions": []})
1259	        return out
1260	    if fit["status"] == "exact":
1261	        points = [fit["solution"]]
1262	    else:
1263	        sigma = 1 if fit["moments"]["covariances"][(2, 3)] > 0 else -1
1264	        points = [_ds_parameters(fit["moments"], r, sigma) for r in fit["root_bracket"]]
1265	    inversions = []
1266	    for params in points:
1267	        gold = (params["false_negatives"][1], params["false_positives"][1])
1268	        controller = (params["false_negatives"][3], params["false_positives"][3])
1269	        rates = asymmetric_gold_noise_inverse(params["prior"], controller, gold, measured["accuracy"],
1270	                                              measured["judge_error"], measured["wrong_wrong_rate"])
1271	        expected = expected_table(size, rates["accuracy"], rates["judge_error"], rates["eps1"])
1272	        table, changed = rounded_table(expected)
1273	        error = declared if declared is not None else rates["judge_error"]
1274	        inversions.append({"parameters": params, "recovered": rates, "corrected_expected": expected,
1275	                           "corrected_table": table, "rounding_changed_a_cell": changed,
1276	                           "tests": _judge_tests(table, error, alpha, declared is None)})
1277	    out.update({"status": fit["status"], "inversions": inversions,
1278	                "bracket_ends_are_a_bracket_only_if_monotone": fit["status"] == "bracketed"})

46	def _as_q(value, name: str) -> Q:
47	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, Q)):
48	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be an int or Fraction, not {type(value).__name__}")

52	def _probability(value, name: str) -> Q:

67	@dataclass(frozen=True)
68	class JudgeTable:
69	    """Counts of a gold-labelled sample by controller right/wrong and judge
70	    right/wrong, both judged against gold.
71	
72	    ``right_right`` (R0): controller right, judge right.
73	    ``right_wrong`` (R1): controller right, judge wrong.
74	    ``wrong_right`` (W0): controller wrong, judge right.
75	    ``wrong_wrong`` (W1): controller wrong, judge wrong.  With binary labels a
76	    judge wrong about a wrong answer marks it correct, so it agrees with it.
77	    """
78	
79	    right_right: int
80	    right_wrong: int
81	    wrong_right: int
82	    wrong_wrong: int
83	
84	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
85	        for field in fields(self):
86	            _count(getattr(self, field.name), field.name)
87	        if self.size < 1:
88	            raise ValueError("the table needs at least one item")
89	
90	    @property
91	    def size(self) -> int:
92	        return self.right_right + self.right_wrong + self.wrong_right + self.wrong_wrong
93	
94	    @property
95	    def controller_right(self) -> int:
96	        return self.right_right + self.right_wrong
97	
98	    @property
99	    def controller_wrong(self) -> int:
100	        return self.wrong_right + self.wrong_wrong
101	
102	    @property
103	    def judge_wrong(self) -> int:
104	        return self.right_wrong + self.wrong_wrong
105	
106	    @property
107	    def agreements(self) -> int:
108	        return self.right_right + self.wrong_wrong
109

111	def table_estimates(table: JudgeTable) -> dict[str, object]:
112	    """Exact plug-in estimates and the bookkeeping identity.
113	
114	    ``eps0_hat`` is undefined when the controller is never right and
115	    ``eps1_hat`` when it is never wrong; the identity is written with
116	    ``2 (1 - a_hat) eps1_hat = 2 W1 / m``, which is defined in every case.
117	    """
118	
119	    m = table.size
120	    a_hat, eps_hat = Q(table.controller_right, m), Q(table.judge_wrong, m)
121	    eps0_hat = Q(table.right_wrong, table.controller_right) if table.controller_right else None
122	    eps1_hat = Q(table.wrong_wrong, table.controller_wrong) if table.controller_wrong else None
123	    agreement = Q(table.agreements, m)
124	    identity_rhs = a_hat - eps_hat + 2 * Q(table.wrong_wrong, m)
125	    inflation = None
126	    if eps0_hat is not None and eps1_hat is not None:
127	        inflation = judge_correlation_inflation(a_hat, eps_hat, eps1_hat)
128	    return {"size": m, "controller_wrong": table.controller_wrong,
129	            "a_hat": a_hat, "eps_hat": eps_hat, "eps0_hat": eps0_hat, "eps1_hat": eps1_hat,
130	            "agreement_rate": agreement, "identity_rhs": identity_rhs,
131	            "identity_holds": agreement == identity_rhs,
132	            "excess_hat": None if eps1_hat is None else eps1_hat - eps_hat,
133	            "inflation_hat": inflation}
134	
135	
136	def agreement_identity_holds(table: JudgeTable) -> bool:
137	    """``(R0 + W1) / m == a_hat - eps_hat + 2 (1 - a_hat) eps1_hat``.
138	
139	    Proof: ``a_hat - eps_hat = (R0 + R1 - R1 - W1) / m = (R0 - W1) / m`` and
140	    ``2 (1 - a_hat) eps1_hat = 2 (W / m)(W1 / W) = 2 W1 / m``; the sum is
141	    ``(R0 + W1) / m``.
142	    """
143	
144	    return table_estimates(table)["identity_holds"]
145	
146	
147	def expected_table(size: int, accuracy, judge_error, eps1) -> dict[str, Q]:
148	    """Expected cell counts, as exact rationals, for a sample of ``size`` items
149	    from a controller of accuracy ``a``, a judge of marginal error ``eps`` and
150	    shared error ``eps1``; ``eps0`` follows from the marginal."""
151	
152	    if type(size) is not int or size < 1:
153	        raise ValueError("size must be a positive integer")
154	    accuracy, judge_error, eps1 = (_probability(accuracy, "accuracy"),
155	                                   _probability(judge_error, "judge_error"),
156	                                   _probability(eps1, "eps1"))
157	    low, high = shared_error_bounds(accuracy, judge_error)
158	    if not low <= eps1 <= high:
159	        raise ValueError("eps1 is infeasible for the marginal judge error")
160	    eps0 = (judge_error - (1 - accuracy) * eps1) / accuracy
161	    return {"right_right": size * accuracy * (1 - eps0),
162	            "right_wrong": size * accuracy * eps0,
163	            "wrong_right": size * (1 - accuracy) * (1 - eps1),
164	            "wrong_wrong": size * (1 - accuracy) * eps1}
165

167	def rounded_table(expected: dict[str, Q]) -> tuple[JudgeTable, bool]:
168	    """Round each expected cell half-up to an integer.  Returns the table and
169	    whether any cell changed; a rounded table may not sum to the planned size."""
170	
171	    cells = {}
172	    for name in ("right_right", "right_wrong", "wrong_right", "wrong_wrong"):
173	        value = _as_q(expected[name], name)
174	        if value < 0:
175	            raise ValueError("expected counts must be nonnegative")
176	        cells[name] = int((value + HALF).__floor__())
177	    changed = any(Q(cells[name]) != expected[name] for name in cells)
178	    return JudgeTable(**cells), changed

# --- 6. four raters: the asymmetric model becomes testable --------------------

RATERS4 = {1: "G1", 2: "G2", 3: "G3", 4: "C"}
PAIRS4 = tuple((i, j) for i in range(1, 5) for j in range(i + 1, 5))
TRIPLES4 = ((1, 2, 3), (1, 2, 4), (1, 3, 4), (2, 3, 4))
CONSTRAINTS4 = ("tetrad_12_34_vs_13_24", "tetrad_13_24_vs_14_23", "third_123_vs_124",
                "third_123_vs_134", "third_123_vs_234", "fourth_moment")
MOMENT_KEYS4 = tuple((i,) for i in range(1, 5)) + PAIRS4 + TRIPLES4 + ((1, 2, 3, 4),)


def _four(values, name: str) -> tuple[Q, Q, Q, Q]:
    if not isinstance(values, (tuple, list)) or len(values) != 4:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must list four rates")
    return tuple(_probability(v, f"{name}[{i}]") for i, v in enumerate(values))


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FourRaterTable:
    """Rational weights on the 2^4 cells ``(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)`` of four binary
    raters' labels: the gold grader G1, a second grader G2, a third grader G3
    and the controller's answer C.  One more independent grading of the same
    sealed sample than ``LabelTable``: that is what a fourth rater costs."""

    cells: dict

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "cells", _weights(self.cells, CELLS4, "(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4) in {0,1}^4"))

    @property
    def total(self) -> Q:
        return sum(self.cells.values(), Q(0))

    def probability(self, cell: tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> Q:
        return self.cells[cell] / self.total

    def triple(self, drop: int) -> LabelTable:
        """Marginal over rater ``drop``; the other three keep their order and
        become raters 1, 2, 3 of a ``LabelTable``."""

        if drop not in (1, 2, 3, 4):
            raise ValueError("drop must name a rater 1..4")
        keep = [i - 1 for i in range(1, 5) if i != drop]
        cells = {cell: Q(0) for cell in CELLS3}
        for cell, weight in self.cells.items():
            cells[tuple(cell[i] for i in keep)] += weight
        return LabelTable(cells)


def _four_cells(prior: Q, sensitivities: tuple, false_positives: tuple) -> dict:
    cells = {}
    for cell in CELLS4:
        weight = Q(0)
        for y in (0, 1):
            w = prior if y else 1 - prior
            for i in range(4):
                hit = sensitivities[i] if y else false_positives[i]
                w *= hit if cell[i] == 1 else 1 - hit
            weight += w
        cells[cell] = weight
    return cells


def four_rater_model(prior, false_negatives, false_positives) -> FourRaterTable:
    """Four conditionally independent raters with asymmetric rates: nine
    parameters ``(pi, alpha_i, beta_i)`` on the fifteen degrees of freedom of
    the 2^4 table, so six constraints (``four_rater_constraints``)."""

    prior = _probability(prior, "prior")
    alphas, betas = _four(false_negatives, "false_negatives"), _four(false_positives, "false_positives")
    return FourRaterTable(_four_cells(prior, tuple(1 - a for a in alphas), betas))


def four_rater_moments(table: FourRaterTable) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Centred moments ``k_S = E prod_{i in S} (X_i - p_i)`` for every subset
    with at least two raters, plus the marginals ``p_i``.  Under the model,
    with ``u = pi (1 - pi)``, ``delta_i = 1 - alpha_i - beta_i`` and
    ``E[X_i - p_i | Y] = delta_i (Y - pi)``: conditional independence gives
    ``k_S = E[(Y - pi)^|S|] prod_{i in S} delta_i`` with ``E[(Y - pi)^2] = u``,
    ``E[(Y - pi)^3] = u (1 - 2 pi)``, ``E[(Y - pi)^4] = u (1 - 3u)``.  So
    ``c_ij = u delta_i delta_j``, ``k_ijk = u (1 - 2 pi) delta_i delta_j
    delta_k`` and ``k_1234 = u (1 - 3u) delta_1 delta_2 delta_3 delta_4``."""

    p = {i: sum((table.probability(c) for c in CELLS4 if c[i - 1] == 1), Q(0)) for i in range(1, 5)}
    moments = {}
    for subset in MOMENT_KEYS4[4:]:
        total = Q(0)
        for cell in CELLS4:
            w = table.probability(cell)
            for i in subset:
                w *= cell[i - 1] - p[i]
            total += w
        moments[subset] = total
    return {"marginals": p, "covariances": {pair: moments[pair] for pair in PAIRS4},
            "third_moments": {t: moments[t] for t in TRIPLES4}, "fourth_moment": moments[(1, 2, 3, 4)]}


def four_rater_residuals(moments: dict) -> dict[str, Q]:
    """The six polynomial equalities, as residuals that vanish under the model.

    Tetrads: ``c_12 c_34 = c_13 c_24 = c_14 c_23`` (each is ``u^2 prod delta``;
    two independent equalities).  Third-moment ratios: ``k_ijk / k_ijl = c_ik
    / c_il = delta_k / delta_l``; written without division, ``k_ijk c_il = k_ijl
    c_ik`` (both are ``u^2 (1 - 2 pi) delta_i^2 delta_j delta_k delta_l``).  Six
    such ratios exist, one per shared pair; given the tetrads three are
    independent, the ones expressing ``k_124, k_134, k_234`` through ``k_123``.
    Fourth moment: ``(k_1234 - c_12 c_34) c_12 = k_123 k_124``, since
    ``k_1234 - c_12 c_34 = u (1 - 4u) prod delta = u (1 - 2 pi)^2 prod delta``
    and ``k_123 k_124 = u^2 (1 - 2 pi)^2 delta_1^2 delta_2^2 delta_3 delta_4``.
    The six have a rank-6 Jacobian in the moments (``constraint_jacobian_rank``)
    and the model's parameter Jacobian has rank 9 on 15 degrees of freedom
    (``four_rater_jacobian_rank``): exactly six independent equalities."""

    c, k, m4 = moments["covariances"], moments["third_moments"], moments["fourth_moment"]
    return {"tetrad_12_34_vs_13_24": c[(1, 2)] * c[(3, 4)] - c[(1, 3)] * c[(2, 4)],
            "tetrad_13_24_vs_14_23": c[(1, 3)] * c[(2, 4)] - c[(1, 4)] * c[(2, 3)],
            "third_123_vs_124": k[(1, 2, 3)] * c[(1, 4)] - k[(1, 2, 4)] * c[(1, 3)],
            "third_123_vs_134": k[(1, 2, 3)] * c[(1, 4)] - k[(1, 3, 4)] * c[(1, 2)],
            "third_123_vs_234": k[(1, 2, 3)] * c[(2, 4)] - k[(2, 3, 4)] * c[(1, 2)],
            "fourth_moment": (m4 - c[(1, 2)] * c[(3, 4)]) * c[(1, 2)] - k[(1, 2, 3)] * k[(1, 2, 4)]}


def constraint_jacobian_rank(moments: dict) -> int:
    """Rank of the 6 x 15 Jacobian of the residuals in the centred moments
    ``(p_i, c_ij, k_ijk, k_1234)``, which are a coordinate system on the
    simplex.  Every residual has degree at most two in each single moment, so
    the central difference ``(r(x + h) - r(x - h)) / 2h`` is the exact partial."""

    flat = {(i,): moments["marginals"][i] for i in range(1, 5)}
    flat.update(moments["covariances"])
    flat.update(moments["third_moments"])
    flat[(1, 2, 3, 4)] = moments["fourth_moment"]

                 "third_moments": {t: values[t] for t in TRIPLES4}, "fourth_moment": values[(1, 2, 3, 4)]}

    h = Q(1)
    columns = []
    for key in MOMENT_KEYS4:

        up[key] += h
        down[key] -= h
        columns.append([(a - b) / (2 * h) for a, b in zip(residuals_at(up), residuals_at(down))])
